♟ Chess

I've Been Playing Chess
Seriously Since JSS1.

And honestly, it became one of the most defining parts of my secondary school story. Chess taught me how to think under pressure, how to plan multiple steps ahead, and how to stay calm when everything is on the line. Here's what six years on the board actually looked like.

🏆
₦1,000,000 Prize Continental Title JSS1 · 2019

African Junior Chess Championship — I Won This in My First Year

I still think about this one a lot. JSS1. First year of secondary school. I entered the African Junior Chess Championship and I won it. Took home a ₦1,000,000 cash prize and a continental title before most of my classmates had even settled into the school routine. It wasn't luck — I had been preparing, I had been studying the game. But winning at that level, at that age, told me something about myself that I've carried ever since.

In the middle of a tournament game — this is what full focus looks like.
🥇 State Champion · 2× Winner

Best Junior Player — Ogun State (2023 & 2025)

The Ogun State Chess Federation recognised me as the best junior chess player in the state twice — in 2023 and again in 2025. Winning it once is something. Coming back two years later and winning it again meant I wasn't peaking — I was still improving.

2023 & 2025 · Ogun State Chess Federation
🥈 National Silver · Team Captain

National Youth Games — I Captained Ogun State

This one meant a lot to me. I was selected to captain the Ogun State chess team at the National Youth Games — a responsibility I did not take lightly. We finished with a team bronze, and I personally took individual silver on my board. Leading a state team at that level while still in secondary school is something I'm genuinely proud of.

2023–2024 · National Youth Games
🥇 3× Consecutive Gold

Redeemed Sports Festival — 5 Finals, 3 Golds Back to Back

Five appearances in the final. My first in 2019 (JSS1) ended in silver — I was just happy to be there. Then from 2023 to 2025, I went back three times and won gold all three times, back to back to back. That run felt different. That was me being the best in the room consistently, not getting lucky once.

2019–2025 · Redeemed Sports Festival
📊 Top 24 in Nigeria

National Blitz Rankings — Top 24 Nationally

As of 2026 I'm ranked in the top 24 blitz chess players in Nigeria. Blitz is fast chess — you have very little time, you have to think quickly and precisely, and there's nowhere to hide. Making the national top 24 in that format means I'm competing at a level most players never reach.

2026 · National Blitz Rankings
🌍 8th Internationally

1st International Jubilee Tournament — Top 10 Finish

I placed 8th in the inaugural International Jubilee Chess Tournament against players from multiple countries. 2020, early in my career. Going up against international competition and finishing in the top 10 confirmed that the African title wasn't a fluke — I could hold my own on any stage.

2020 · International Jubilee Tournament
🏅 4th Nationally

1st National Nwanga Chess Tournament — 4th Place

Placed 4th in the first-ever National Nwanga Chess Tournament. A brand new competition, a national field of serious players, and I finished 4th. No prior knowledge of the format, no advantage — just preparation and adaptability.

National Nwanga Chess Tournament
🎓
I Also Coached Chess at School — For Free

I was the best chess player in my school, but I never used that to make myself feel above people. I voluntarily coached students — inside and outside school hours, completely free — because I genuinely wanted them to love the game the way I do. Teaching chess is harder than playing it. You have to understand it deeply enough to explain it simply. I think I did that.

🎖 Leadership

From Library Prefect
to Head Boy.

Leadership found me early — or maybe I went looking for it. Either way, every role I held came with real responsibility, and I took every single one seriously. The progression from SS1 to SS3 tells its own story.

👑

Head Boy — SS3

2025

The highest student position in the school. I was the one staff came to when things needed to be addressed, the one students came to when they had problems, and the one who had to hold it all together while still studying, competing, and finishing as top of my class. It was a lot — and I loved every bit of it.

🧑‍💼

Assistant Head Boy — SS2

2024

The year before the top role. I was already embedded in school governance — handling discipline, student representation, and supporting the Head Boy. It was preparation in the best way. By the time SS3 came, I already knew exactly what the job required.

📚

Library Prefect — SS1

2023

Where it started. I managed the school library — organising materials, maintaining order, creating an environment where people actually wanted to read. Not the flashiest role, but I took it seriously. Every big position I held later was built on treating this one with the same care.

🎤

Won the Debate Competition

2024

I've always been able to hold my ground in an argument — but debate is different. You have to research, structure, anticipate counter-arguments, and stay composed in front of a crowd. I won the intra-school debate competition in 2024, and honestly it's one of the achievements I don't think gets enough credit on this page.

📰

Press Club — 6 Years

2019–2025

This is the one that ran the whole way through — six straight years with the Press Club, from my very first year to my very last. Covering school events, writing reports, helping shape how the school's stories got told. While other commitments started and ended, this one was constant. It taught me how to observe, document, and communicate clearly — skills that show up in everything else on this page.

🎵 Music

Three Instruments.
I Learned Most of This Myself.

Music was never a subject for me — it was just something I was genuinely into. I picked up the saxophone first, then taught myself guitar, then added piano. By SS3 I was Lead Instrumentalist and coordinating the brigade. Here's the full picture.

🎷
Saxophone
My main instrument. I performed with this at school events, ceremonies, live gigs, and brigade performances. By 2025 I was the Lead Instrumentalist.
🎸
Guitar
Self-taught. No classes, no instructor — just me, YouTube, and a lot of patience. I wanted to learn it so I learned it. Simple as that.
🎹
Piano
Picked this up alongside the others. Played at school events and ceremonies — added a different dimension to my performances.

💼 Business

I Was Running Real Money
Before Most People Start.

I've always had an eye for gaps — things that aren't there but should be, things that could work but nobody's tried. In secondary school, I didn't just have ideas. I acted on them. Two real businesses, real clients, real revenue — all while going to school.

Family Business — I Ran This for About 3 Years
Full operations management · Supply chain · B2B sales
₦5,000,000+ Revenue

I wasn't helping with the family business — I was running it. Sourcing goods from suppliers across Nigeria, coordinating logistics, managing client relationships with hotels and lounges, and being fully accountable for every unit of stock in and out. The business did over ₦5 million in revenue during that period. I did all of this while attending school, sitting exams, competing in chess, and holding leadership roles. Sleep was optional sometimes. That's just how it was.

🔗
Supply Chain
I sourced from multiple suppliers across Nigeria and handled cross-country logistics. Nobody was doing it for me — I figured it out.
🤝
B2B Sales
My clients were hotels and lounges. I had to show up professional, negotiate properly, and maintain those relationships over time.
📊
Full Accountability
Every unit in, every unit out — I was responsible. There was no one to blame if something went wrong. That kind of accountability changes you.
🌙
Night Hustle
Some of the best selling happened late. I stayed out for it, then went home and did my school work. Discipline over comfort, every time.
🏫 School Stationery Business — I Did This for 5 Years

This one started simple. I noticed students and teachers constantly needed stationery and there was no easy way to get it within school. So I started selling it myself. What began as a small hustle turned into a five-year operation — consistent, profitable, and growing. I served both students and staff, I understood my customer base, and I kept showing up. Five years is not a coincidence. That's a business.

🔧 Builds & Initiatives

If It Didn't Exist,
I Built It.

I don't really know how to see a problem and just ignore it. If something wasn't working, or something was missing, my default response was to figure out how to fix it or build it myself. Hardware, software, education, craft — the range surprised even me.

⏰
I Built 10 Clocks for My School
Hardware

Classrooms had no working clocks. Nobody was doing anything about it. So I built 10 functional wall clocks from local materials and put them up in classrooms myself. No budget, no instruction from anyone. Just a problem that needed solving and me deciding to solve it.

🤖
Built an AI Learning Website for My School
Software

I developed an AI-powered learning website specifically for my school community. The idea was to make academic content more accessible — especially for students who didn't have extra resources at home. I built it while I was still a student there. Still proud of this one.

📱
Brought My School Online
Digital

My school had no social media presence. Zero visibility online. I pushed for it, created the accounts, and got it off the ground. It wasn't assigned to me — I just thought it needed to exist, so I made it exist.

💻
I Taught People to Code
Education

I introduced programming to people of all ages — young kids, classmates, older adults — inside and outside school. Programming gets treated like something reserved for a certain type of person. I don't believe that. I wanted to show people it's learnable, and that's exactly what I did.

👟
TheKing's Fit — My Own Brand
Craft / Brand

I spent two years learning how to make shoes alongside school. Not for any assignment or credit — I just wanted to learn a craft and build something with my hands. I made and sold slippers under my own brand, TheKing's Fit. If you know me personally, you know I actually wore some of them too.

🎓 Academics

And Through All of That —
I Was Still Number One.

Everything you just read — chess tournaments, businesses, leadership, music, builds — all of it happened while I was still the top academic student in my school. 3.9 GPA. 6 awards at graduation. A JAMB score nobody had hit in 26 years. The academics weren't separate from everything else. They were part of the same thing.

Graduation day — sitting with all 6 awards. That's what six years of not taking shortcuts looks like.
📜
🏅 School Record 26-Year First 2025

I Scored 330 in JAMB — First to Break 300 in My School's 26-Year History

No student in the school had crossed 300 in JAMB in 26 years. I scored 330. I didn't know it was a record when I sat the exam — I just prepared as hard as I could and went in to do my best. When the results came out and people started talking about what it meant historically, it hit differently. That record had been standing since before I was born. I broke it.

🎤
Top of Class

Valedictorian

I gave the valedictory speech at graduation. I stood at that podium as the person the class chose to represent them — and I was proud of every word I said. It's one of those moments that doesn't fully make sense until it's actually happening.

📊
Academic Excellence

3.9 GPA

Across all six years of secondary school. Not just one good year — the whole run. People always ask how I managed everything at once. Honestly, I just never gave myself the option to let the grades slip. Everything else had to work around that.

🥇
Class of 2025

Ranked #001

First in my graduating class. Not just among friends or in my set — in the entire year. I'm not going to downplay that. It took work, consistency, and a lot of late nights. But it's there, it's official, and it belongs to me.

🏆
6 Awards at Graduation — Same Night
Class of 2025 · Secondary School Graduation Ceremony
🎤 Valedictorian Award 📊 Best Academic Performance 🥇 Best Graduating Student ♟ Best in Extracurriculars 🌟 Most Outstanding Student 🎓 Overall Best Student

Six awards. One night. I still have them all.

📐

MAN Maths Competition

2025

Dominated the Mathematical Association of Nigeria competition at school level. Maths has always come naturally to me — but the MAN competition tests depth, not just speed. I enjoyed it a lot more than I probably should have.

🔢

Olympiad Maths — Made it to State Level

2025

Advanced to state level in the Olympian Mathematics competition — you have to beat your school, then your district, to get there. The Olympiad doesn't test what you were taught. It tests how you think. Getting to state level in that environment meant something to me.

Six years. One school. No regrets.

I'm currently on a gap year — thinking, building, and figuring out what comes next. This page is a record of where I've been. The next chapter is still being written.
